text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, continuing a pullback from its recent peak of $137.20 two days ago. The decline comes despite oil prices holding firm—US crude at $91.48 and world oil at $96.02—suggesting the stock's weakness reflects profit-taking after a sharp rally rather than deteriorating fundamentals in the energy market itself. Over the past week, the stock has swung between gains and losses as traders weigh competing signals.

The broader context is mixed for oil majors. While geopolitical tensions between Iran and the U.S. have pushed crude prices to six-week highs and gasoline has hit record levels above $4 per gallon, those same elevated pump prices fuel political pressure and consumer pushback—forces that can weigh on energy stocks over time. The Trump administration's new Venezuela oil deal and ongoing Middle East friction keep crude supported, but the stock's recent volatility suggests investors are uncertain whether these price gains will stick or whether energy demand might soften.
